message.content:
Below is a complete, ready‑to‑run example that shows **two** ways to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS:

| Method | What you run | Why it works |
|--------|--------------|--------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | The most common, easiest way if you already have the Cloud SDK installed. |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances` | Useful if you want to embed the call in a script, CI/CD pipeline, or a custom UI. |

> **Important**  
> * The **GPU API** (`compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/.../zones/.../instances`) must be enabled for your project.  
> * You must have a **service account** or OAuth token with the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role (or equivalent).  
> * The **GPU quota** for the RTX A6000 must be available in the zone you choose.  

---

## 1. gcloud CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports RTX A6000
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
DISK_SIZE_GB=100
DISK_TYPE="pd-standard"      # or pd-ssd for higher performance
NETWORK="default"

# 2️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "rtx-a6000-ubuntu20" \
  --project="${PROJECT}" \
  --zone="${ZONE}" \
  --machine-type="${MACHINE_TYPE}" \
  --accelerator="type=${GPU_TYPE},count=${GPU_COUNT}" \
  --image-family="${IMAGE_FAMILY}" \
  --image-project="${IMAGE_PROJECT}" \
  --boot-disk-size="${DISK_SIZE_GB}GB" \
  --boot-disk-type="${DISK_TYPE}" \
  --network="${NETWORK}" \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags http-server,https-server \
  --scopes "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM configuration |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | Disk size & type |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: runs a shell script on first boot (e.g., install NVIDIA drivers) |
| `--tags` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules if you need them |
| `--scopes` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access (adjust as needed) |

> **Tip** – If you want to install the NVIDIA driver automatically, create a `startup.sh` file with something like:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
sudo reboot
```

---

## 2. REST API (JSON)

Below is a minimal JSON payload you can POST to the Compute Engine API. Replace placeholders (`{project}`, `{zone}`) with your actual values.

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu20",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nsudo reboot"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### How to POST it

```bash
# 1️⃣  Get an OAuth 2.0 access token (replace YOUR_TOKEN with a real token)
TOKEN="YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"

# 2️⃣  POST the JSON
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

> **Note** – The `acceleratorType` URL must match the zone you’re using.  
> **Tip** – Use `gcloud auth print-access-token` to quickly get a token if you have the SDK installed.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | GPU quota for RTX A6000 in chosen zone |
| ✅ | GPU API enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`) |
| ✅ | Service account / OAuth token with `compute.instanceAdmin.v1` |
| ✅ | Correct machine type (CPU/RAM) for your workload |
| ✅ | Proper disk type & size |
| ✅ | Optional: startup script to install NVIDIA drivers |

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu20@<external-ip>
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version. Happy computing!
